questions.prompt: A React form component renders several times on one page and needs distinct label/input ID pairs. Which API is intended for this purpose?

choices.text: useId
A random render-time value.
An array index reused as the same DOM identifier in every form instance.
A random value computed independently during server and client rendering.

questions.explanation: useId supplies unique IDs for accessibility relationships. Render-time counters and independently generated random IDs can break stability or hydration matching.

sources.title: useId – React
sources.claim: useId creates accessibility IDs, is not for list keys, and supports consistent server/client IDs when the component trees match.

questions.prompt: A React tooltip must measure its rendered size and correct its position before the user sees that frame. Which effect timing supports this?

choices.text: useEffect after paint.
useLayoutEffect before paint.
A server-only Effect that reads the final client viewport during SSR.
A useMemo callback that reads committed DOM nodes while rendering.

questions.explanation: useLayoutEffect can measure after DOM placement and update before repaint. It blocks paint, so expensive work in it can harm responsiveness.

sources.title: useLayoutEffect – React
sources.claim: useLayoutEffect runs before browser paint and blocks repaint; effects do not run on the server, where layout information is unavailable.

questions.prompt: A React component uses useImperativeHandle to expose focus and scroll methods. Which statements are accurate? Select all that apply.

choices.text: In React 19, a function component can receive ref as a prop.
The hook automatically exposes every internal state setter to the parent.
An empty dependency list guarantees methods capture future state values.
The handle may expose methods instead of the entire DOM node.
Reactive values used to build the handle belong in its dependency list.

questions.explanation: A is correct: React 19 supports the ref prop; older versions use forwardRef for this pattern. B is incorrect: only the returned handle is exposed. C is incorrect: unchanged handles retain their closures unless they use another current-value mechanism. D is correct: the hook customizes the ref value and can restrict its public API. E is correct: dependencies control recreating the handle with current closures.

sources.title: useImperativeHandle – React
sources.claim: useImperativeHandle customizes the value exposed through a ref; reactive dependencies govern rebuilding the handle; React 19 permits ref as a prop.

questions.prompt: A React list contains records with stable database IDs. A developer proposes calling useId to generate each list key. What should the review recommend?

choices.text: Use a new random key on each render.
Replace every record key with one useId shared by the whole list component.
Use the records' stable IDs as keys.
Generate a different random key on every render to keep the rows distinct.

questions.explanation: useId is for IDs used in accessibility relationships, not list keys. Keys should come from stable data; calling Hooks in a variable-length map also breaks Hook ordering.

sources.title: useId – React
sources.claim: useId creates accessibility IDs, is not for list keys, and supports consistent server/client IDs when the component trees match.

questions.prompt: A React server-rendering component depends on useLayoutEffect to measure element geometry. What limitation must its author handle?

choices.text: Server Effects read the client viewport.
React serializes the client viewport into every server Effect automatically.
useLayoutEffect runs on the server but useEffect alone is client-only.
The server has no layout information.

questions.explanation: Effects run on the client. The server cannot supply browser layout measurements, so server rendering must use a suitable fallback or defer that component until the client.

sources.title: useLayoutEffect – React
sources.claim: useLayoutEffect runs before browser paint and blocks repaint; effects do not run on the server, where layout information is unavailable.

questions.prompt: A React 19 input wrapper returns a small imperative handle from useImperativeHandle. Which design claims hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: React 19 ref-as-prop support also makes this pattern work unchanged in React 18.
The parent sees the returned handle through its ref.
A changed dependency can cause React to create a new handle.
Returning a focus method causes React to invoke it during every render.
The hook requires the handle to be a DOM element and forbids plain objects.

questions.explanation: A is incorrect: earlier React versions need forwardRef to receive the ref. B is correct: the returned object is the customized ref value. C is correct: Object.is comparison of the dependency list governs re-execution. D is incorrect: the parent or other caller invokes the exposed method explicitly. E is incorrect: custom objects containing methods are a standard use case.

sources.title: useImperativeHandle – React
sources.claim: useImperativeHandle customizes the value exposed through a ref; reactive dependencies govern rebuilding the handle; React 19 permits ref as a prop.
